name: avatar
title: Avatar
description: People in comments, assignees, and member lists.
docs:
## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/avatar ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge @base-ui/react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | avatar | `@components/cadence/avatar/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/avatar.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: avatar](https://cadence.dev/r/avatar.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Keep `avatar/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` at the listed relative paths so the shared `cn` import resolves. Preserve the component's `"use client"` directive: `@base-ui/react/avatar` manages image loading, errors and fallback visibility after hydration. Avatar is T0 and has no authored animation in full, reduced or none mode; no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required. `AvatarBadge`, `AvatarGroup` and `AvatarGroupCount` are exports from the same Avatar file. Use them directly from the Usage import path; no separate Badge or group component installation is needed. Include `AvatarFallback` with meaningful initials and supply image `alt` text, or `alt=""` when an adjacent name already identifies the person. Give a meaningful presence badge a text alternative such as the `sr-only` span in Presence, including when the small size hides its icon. Usage needs your own `/ada.png`. Image and fallback uses an external GitHub image, deliberately invalid image data to demonstrate failure, and an avatar without an image. Replace those sources with your own assets; Base UI switches between image and fallback without a cross-fade. The top preview uses inline SVG portrait data, initials and a presence dot with a native `sr-only` span. Sizes and Group use initials only. These examples need no additional npm packages or registry items; the site's preview frame is not part of the consumer setup. The Presence example additionally imports `CheckIcon` from `lucide-react`. Install it only when copying that example; it is not an Avatar dependency: ```package-manager npm install lucide-react ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarImage } from "@/components/cadence/avatar"; export function Author() { return ( AL ); } ``` ## Sizes `size` sets `data-size` on each root. Small, default and large are 24, 32 and 40 CSS pixels; children follow their own root rather than a shared page setting. ```tsx import { Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage, } from "@/components/cadence/avatar"; export function AvatarSizes() { return (
{(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => ( AL ))}
); } ``` ## Image and fallback Always include a fallback. The first avatar shows initials while its image loads, then the image replaces them. The second deliberately supplies invalid image bytes to demonstrate an error; the third has no image at all. Base UI owns this loading state and swaps content without a cross-fade. ```tsx import { Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage, } from "@/components/cadence/avatar"; export function AvatarImageAndFallback() { return (
SC Image
GH Failed image
AL No image
); } ``` ## Presence A badge is static presence feedback, not a loading pulse. Its dot follows the root size; a supplied icon is hidden at the smallest size. Keep a text alternative even when the icon disappears. ```tsx import { CheckIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage, } from "@/components/cadence/avatar"; export function AvatarPresence() { return (
{(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => ( AL Online ))}
); } ``` ## Group Group overlaps a short list and leaves overflow counting to the caller. Give all members of a group the same size; the count tile follows that group. These three independent groups show the supported sizes without linking their state. ```tsx import { Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage, } from "@/components/cadence/avatar"; export function AvatarGroups() { return (
{(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => ( AL GH KJ +3 ))}
); } ``` ## When to use - A person or an entity next to content they own: a comment, an assignee, a commit. - A stack of participants, with a `+3` tile for the rest. - A presence indicator on a collaborator, via `AvatarBadge`. ## When not to use - A logo that must stay legible at small sizes; use the image with a fixed box. - A decorative illustration; avatars imply a person or an account. - More than about five faces. Past that the stack stops being readable — use `AvatarGroupCount` with a name list in the tooltip. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `Avatar` | `size`, Base UI root props | `size`: `"default" \| "sm" \| "lg"`. Sets `data-size`. | | `AvatarImage` | Base UI image props | `src`, `alt`. Hidden automatically when the image fails. | | `AvatarFallback` | Base UI fallback props | Rendered while loading and after an error. | | `AvatarBadge` | native span props | Corner dot; sized from the root's `data-size`. | | `AvatarGroup` | native div props | Overlapping stack with a ring in the page colour. | | `AvatarGroupCount` | native div props | The `+3` tile that closes a stack. | All parts carry `data-slot`, so `[&>[data-slot=avatar]]:size-6` style overrides are possible without a prop. Root, Image and Fallback accept Base UI state callbacks for `className` and `style`. Caller classes merge last; Badge and group parts use native string classes and object styles. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). The image-to-fallback swap is instant by design: Base UI knows when the image errored, and a cross-fade would show a half-drawn face in the meantime. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - `AvatarImage` is an ``: always pass a real `alt`. With a name beside the avatar, use `alt=""` so it is not announced twice. - `AvatarFallback` prints initials. Those initials are the accessible name when the image is missing, so derive them from the person's actual name. - `AvatarBadge` is a visual dot. Give it a text alternative when the presence state matters — e.g. `Online` inside it, or an `aria-label` on the badge. - An avatar that links to a profile must be wrapped in an `` with an accessible name; the image `alt` alone is not a link name. ## Responsiveness and performance Avatar sizes are explicit rather than breakpoint-driven. Groups overlap avatars; the caller limits the visible count and supplies overflow text. Base UI owns image loading and fallback state after hydration. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Always render an `AvatarFallback`; without it a failed image leaves an empty hole. - Do not animate the presence dot. State lives in the DOM (`aria-label`, text), not in a pulse.
